title: Finite prime decomposition of principal radicals in a normalization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] that is a domain, meaning $1
e0$ and $xy=0$ implies $x=0$ or $y=0$. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ for the field of quotients $a/b$ with $a,b\in R$ and $b
e0$. Let $F/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning $F$ has finite dimension over $K$, and let $D\subseteq F$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every $0
e b\in D$, there exist finitely many prime ideals $Q_1,\ldots,Q_t$ of $D$ such that $\sqrt{bD}=Q_1\cap\cdots\cap Q_t$. Here $\sqrt{bD}=\{x\in D:x^m\in bD	ext{ for some }m\ge1\}$, and the intersection for $t=0$ is $D$. No Noetherian-ring or module-finiteness hypothesis on $D$ is imposed.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules, Definition 4.10.1, Proposition 4.10.3 and Theorem 4.10.5 (Mori–Nagata), printed pp. 89–91; finite-extension reduction as in Proposition 4.8.5, printed p. 85. Read online in the author-hosted book at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a finite $K$-basis $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m$ of $F$. For each $i$, linear dependence of $1,\alpha_i,\ldots,\alpha_i^{m}$ over $K$ gives a monic relation $\alpha_i^{n_i}+\sum_{j<n_i}c_{ij}\alpha_i^j=0$ with $n_i\ge1$ and $c_{ij}\in K$. Choose $0\ne d_i\in R$ divisible by the finitely many denominators of the $c_{ij}$. Then $\beta_i=d_i\alpha_i$ satisfies the monic relation $\beta_i^{n_i}+\sum_{j<n_i}(d_i^{n_i-j}c_{ij})\beta_i^j=0$ over $R$, since $n_i-j\ge1$ and $d_ic_{ij}\in R$. Thus each $\beta_i$ is integral over $R$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.8.2, printed p. 84 (finite field-extension reduction via a finite integral subring); explicit denominator scaling of monic relations.

proof.text: Put $S=R[\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m]\subseteq F$. It is a domain because it is a subring of the field $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] it is a finite $R$-module, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes $S$ integral over $R$. Its displayed finite algebra generating set and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] make $S$ Noetherian. Its fraction field is $F$: the fraction field of $S$ contains $K$ and each $\alpha_i=\beta_i/d_i$, hence contains every $K$-linear combination of the basis elements; the opposite inclusion holds since $S\subseteq F$.

source.place: Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral, (3) implies (1); Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: The integral closure of $S$ in $F$ equals $D$. If $x\in D$, its monic equation over $R$ is also over $S$, so it lies in that closure. Conversely, if $x\in F$ is integral over $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] applied to $S[x]$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] show that $S[x]$ is integral over $S$. As $S$ is integral over $R$ by Step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] gives integrality of $S[x]$ over $R$, so $x\in D$. This proves both inclusions without assuming either normalization finite.

source.place: Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral; Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; Tag 00GN, lemma-integral-transitive (the integral-closure identification is written out).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-integral-closure-krull] to the Noetherian domain $S$ and its own fraction field $F$ verified in Step 2. Its integral closure in that field is $D$ by Step 3, so $D$ is a Krull domain. The theorem is used only in its own-fraction-field form.

For $0\ne b\in D$, [lem-trf-krull-principal-primary-decomposition] gives the finite list $P_1,\ldots,P_t$ of height-one primes containing $b$, and the ideals $J_i=D\cap bD_{P_i}$, with $bD=\bigcap_iJ_i$ and $\sqrt{J_i}=P_i$. All hypotheses hold by Step 4; no ring-Noetherianity of $D$ has been asserted.

For $x\in\sqrt{bD}$, a positive power of $x$ belongs to every $J_i$, hence $x\in\sqrt{J_i}=P_i$. Conversely, if $x\in\bigcap_iP_i$, choose $n_i\ge1$ with $x^{n_i}\in J_i$. For the nonempty finite list put $n=\max_i n_i$; ideal closure under multiplication gives $x^n\in J_i$ for every $i$, hence $x^n\in\bigcap_iJ_i=bD$. This proves $\sqrt{bD}=\bigcap_iP_i$. If the list is empty, Step 5 says $bD=D$, so its radical is $D$, also the empty intersection. Taking $Q_i=P_i$ proves every clause, including a unit $b$ in any domain and the field case.

source.place: Proposition 4.10.3, printed p. 89; the finite radical/intersection calculation is explicit and elementary.

from.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.2 proof, final finite-type alternative: Heinzer’s Corollary for the normalization of a Noetherian integral domain supplies the Noetherian normalization spectrum. Algebraic input for the Noetherian induction proving the Heinzer normalization assertion.

split_report.summary: Wrote six proof steps: scale a finite field basis to integral elements; construct a finite integral Noetherian model S with fraction field F using existing Mathlib leaves; identify its normalization with D by transitivity; apply the own-fraction-field Mori–Nagata theorem; obtain the Krull principal-primary decomposition; and prove the radical equality by taking a maximum of the finitely many exponents. Created only the two non-elementary structural theorem nodes, neither a restatement of the item. Statement unchanged. No new Mathlib leaves.
